channel.title: NoteFlowAI project releases
channel.description: New features with verified releases and usage documentation.

item.title: fix: fail the diff gate when the baseline run did not finish
item.description:
evalarc diff and the GitHub Action now fail the gate (exit 1) when the baseline run did not finish. Before this change, an Inspect baseline log whose status was not success could pass. Checks missing from it were classified as 'added', and 'added' never blocks. Change classification, counts and blocking rules are unchanged. When the baseline is incomplete, diff.json gains "baseline_incomplete": true and gate_passed is false. When the baseline is complete, the key is left out, so those reports keep their previous content apart from created_at and version.
After the existing summary line, default stdout prints: 'The baseline run is incomplete (status error); N check(s) appear only in the current run and were not compared. Rerun the baseline to completion; the gate fails.'
summary.md and --markdown add a line below the table: 'The baseline run did not finish (status `error`); the gate fails because checks missing from it cannot be compared. N check(s) appear only in the current run. Rerun the baseline to completion.' The heading reads 'EvalArc: the baseline run is incomplete' only when there are no blocking changes and the current run finished. Otherwise it shows the existing blocking heading or 'the baseline and current runs are incomplete'.
index.html shows 'Gate failed' with the reason 'the baseline run is incomplete'. When there are no blocking rows, it says 'Rerun the baseline to completion and compare again.' evalarc verify recomputes the same result. docs/ci-gate.md and the README CI-gate paragraph document the rule.
The controller ran the checks; the author did not run anything. On base commit dc848cc, tests/test_feature_f107c0a41d3a.py failed (5 failed, 1 passed), which confirms the gap. On candidate bc6089b, these all exited 0: the feature test, the full pytest suite, ruff check, ruff format --check, scripts/build_site.py and node scripts/check_site.cjs.

item.title: record the Git source commit in MCP open_skill receipts
item.description: On candidate commit 59390b7, a successful MCP open_skill call that passes its expected_sha256 and expected_bundle_sha256 checks now returns structuredContent.receipt.source_commit. For a skill from a Git source, it is the 40-character lowercase HEAD SHA of that source's cache checkout at load time. For agent directories, plugin marketplaces and extra local directories it is null, and no Git command runs for them. For a Git source whose commit cannot be proven, it is also null and the server logs one 'skills-anywhere: source commit unavailable for <name>: <reason>' warning. That covers Git missing or failing, a timeout, or a work tree with no .git of its own or one outside the cache. The load still returns unchanged content in that case. Git runs without a shell and with GIT_* variables removed. Discovery stops at the cache directory, so the commit of an enclosing repository is never reported. Rejected loads throw their existing errors before any Git lookup. The advertised outputSchema declares source_commit. The schema string stays skills-anywhere-load-1. These are unchanged: loadReceipt(), LoadReceipt, OpenedSkill, the exported openSkill(), dsh provider and tool receipts, skill:// resources and rendered text. Controller-run checks on 59390b7: an acceptance-before run failed 3/3 feature tests because the receipt had only 11 fields. After the change, pnpm run build passed. tests/test_feature_ea6b51801ed9.test.ts passed. pnpm run check passed, and its log shows 24 test files and 245 tests passing. pnpm run showcase:build and pnpm run showcase:check also passed.

item.title: count final Bedrock chat failures by cause on the dashboard
item.description:
Version 1.53.0 makes failed Amazon Bedrock chat calls visible on the existing admin dashboard. The Usage today card has a fourth metric, Failed requests. The seven-day usage panel has one line, for example 'Failed chat requests, last 7 days: 4. Throttled 3, access denied 1.' When there are none it reads 'No failed chat requests recorded in the last 7 days.' The line also appears in the existing empty state. A site where every call fails no longer looks like a quiet site.
A failure is counted once per handle_chat_message() or stream_chat_message() call, only if that call sent at least one Bedrock HTTP request and still returned an error after fallback and Converse adaptation retries. AI_Chat_Bedrock_Usage::classify_failure() sorts it into one of six categories using the HTTP status and the plugin error code: throttled (429), access_denied (401/403), validation (400), unavailable (5xx), network (status 0 with aicfab_unreachable or aicfab_stream_interrupted) or other.
Some cases are not counted: - Missing credentials, an invalid region or model, the daily limit, and encoding errors. None of these send a request. - Retries that later succeeded. - Stopped streams.
Only per-day category counts are stored in the existing ai_chat_bedrock_usage option. No message, prompt, output, error text, user ID or IP is kept. Requests, tokens, per-model counts and the daily cap still count successful invocations only.
Controller-run checks on commit d1da36b: - Before the change, the new test failed with exit 255 (undefined classify_failure) on the base code. - tests/test_feature_364f48c382c4.php passed with assertions enabled. - bin/prerelease.sh passed: 47 suites including usage.php and admin-ux.php, phpcs clean, and versions all 1.53.0. - tests/tooling.php passed. - bin/build-package.py built the 1.53.0 zip.
The stream_chat_message() return-path check that failed in the prior review now passes.

item.title: fix: name the first bad frame in LeRobot timeline errors
item.description: robot-reel lerobot now names the first frame that breaks an episode's timeline. It still stops with exit status 2 and writes no output. Each message gives the dataset-relative data file, the episode and the first bad frame_index. There are five cases: a missing frame (with the next recorded frame_index), a repeated frame, an unexpected value (negative, null, NaN or non-numeric), a frame with no finite timestamp, and a timestamp that is not after the previous frame's (both values shown). Frame indices are now checked before the metadata length check, so a frame dropped mid-episode is reported as a gap instead of a count mismatch. A missing final frame keeps the old 'Episode metadata lists N frames but ... holds N-1' message. Every timeline message ends with 'Robot Reel does not reorder, fill or interpolate frames; repair or re-export the episode.' The accept/reject rule is unchanged, so float or bool frame_index columns equal to 0..length-1 are still accepted. docs/lerobot.md has a new 'Timeline errors' section. Controller results for commit f8e0c1e: before the fix, the new test file ran 10 tests on the base code with 5 failures (the old generic messages) and 5 skips. After the fix, one gated run passed the new test file, the full Python unittest suite, npm run check:js, node --test (52 of 52) and robot_reel.pages --write (0 files updated). I wrote this delivery text only; I did not run any of these checks myself.

item.title: claim-audit worksheet for recently published numeric claims (RA-01)
item.description:
Adds python3 -m pairadar.claims, an offline, read-only command for the RA-01 claim review. It reads the published JSON Feed store (radar/feed.json by default). For each figure in the items[]._radar entries within the chosen window, it prints one row of a deterministic Markdown review sheet. The columns are #, day, evidence, claim, status, context, source and an empty review cell. Each status comes from distill.number_context applied to the stored text: - quoted: the figure was found in the stored excerpt. - title: the figure was found only in the title. - no-excerpt: the stored excerpt is empty, as it is for baseline entries. - unlocated: the figure is not in the stored title or truncated excerpt. Check the original source first.
The reference day is the newest valid entry date, not the system clock. The header gives the store path, reference day, days, total figures T, rows shown S and skipped entries K. A whole-window status-count line always appears. When the sheet is capped, a line gives the number of hidden unlocated and no-excerpt figures and a --limit T rerun value. Items that are not objects, lack a _radar dict or have a non-canonical date are skipped and counted. Store problems (missing, unreadable or invalid JSON, wrong shape or version, no dated entries) exit 2 with one 'claims: ' stderr line and no traceback.
Controller-executed checks on candidate 3bd0c4f: - The feature test ran on the pre-change tree and failed with ImportError because pairadar.claims did not exist yet. - On the candidate, python -m pairadar --rerender --no-readme exited 0. - tests/test_feature_02985cec3631.py exited 0. - The full unittest suite passed: 469 tests, OK.
The author did not run any of these checks.

item.title: fix: fail the diff gate when a check has fewer assessed attempts than the baseline
item.description:
evalarc diff now has a blocking change kind, less_covered. A check gets it when the current run assessed fewer attempts than the baseline and the pass rate did not fall. A smaller sample can no longer be reported as improved or unchanged. For example, 2/2 to 1/1, 1/2 to 1/1, and 2/2 to 1/1 with one unassessed attempt are all less_covered, and the command exits 1. The existing kinds still take precedence. A lower pass rate is still reported as regressed or less_reliable. A check that passed before and now has zero assessed attempts is still unassessed. The CLI now reads its list of blocking kinds from BLOCKING, so it prints lines such as ' less_covered: cancel-pending / match'. With --output, diff.json keeps schema evalarc.results-diff.v1 and lists less_covered in counts and changes. summary.md shows a 'less covered' row with the baseline and current fractions, and the index.html row uses the existing failed styling. Comparisons where no check lost assessed attempts give the same results as before. docs/ci-gate.md and docs/ci-gate.zh-CN.md list less_covered in the change table.
Controller-executed checks on image sha256:3effc5c7...: On base commit e99bc9e, the new tests/test_feature_3412504c3ce6.py failed 6 of 15 tests. The trimmed comparison exited 0 and reported 'Unchanged: 16', which confirms the gap. On candidate commit d4a4afd, all of the following exited 0: that test file, the full pytest suite (including the unchanged tests/test_results_diff.py), ruff check, ruff format --check, scripts/build_site.py and node scripts/check_site.cjs. The earlier review finding that ruff format --check would fail is resolved by that passing run. I did not run these checks myself.

item.title: score keyword lane classification against a labeled shortlist
item.description:
python3 -m pairadar.lanes has a new --labels PATH option. It compares the keyword lane classifier with a hand-labeled JSON file. For each entry it scores title + '. ' + summary using ranked_lanes, whose top lane is the one distill.classify picks. It then applies the existing thin/ambiguous rules. Those rules now live in a flag_reasons helper that inspect() also calls.
The command prints a JSON report with: - labels: the file's basename only - labeled and margin - agreement for all, confident (unflagged) and flagged entries, each as n, agree and rate (rate is null when n is 0) - disagreements in input order, each with id (null when absent), title, label, predicted, reasons, best and runner_up
A disagreement with reasons [] is a confident misfile that the flags missed.
The whole file is validated before anything is scored. Invalid input exits 2 with one 'lanes: ' stderr line and empty stdout. This covers an unreadable file, invalid JSON or non-UTF-8 text, no items list, a non-object entry, an empty or non-string title or lane, a non-string id or summary, an unknown lane (the valid ids are listed), and combining --labels with --latest or --fail-on-suspicious. In labels mode the exit code is 0 whenever a report is printed. docs/METHODOLOGY.md section 9 documents the format and its limits.
The controller ran the checks, not me. In the pre-feature run, 8 of the 10 feature tests errored because argparse rejected --labels. On candidate c109acf the controller ran python -m pairadar --rerender --no-readme (exit 0), the 10 feature tests (all passed) and the full unittest suite (446 tests, OK).

item.title: choose the content gaps period and export the same window
item.description:
The Content gaps card on the Conversations screen now has a Period control with Last 7 days, Last 30 days and Last 90 days, plus a Show button. The form does not submit when the select changes. After Show, the summary sentence, the gap table and the empty state cover the chosen window. The empty state names the window and suggests trying a longer period.
The period carries over to the Stored exchanges filter, pagination and the Reset link. Reset clears only the log search, source and rating. At 30 days, including when invalid input falls back to 30, none of those forms or URLs gain aicfab_gap_days, and Reset is the plain page URL, as in 1.47.6.
Download content gaps CSV exports the window shown on screen. Seven-day and 90-day files are named ai-chat-bedrock-content-gaps-7d-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.csv and ...-90d-.... A 30-day file, or one with a missing or rejected period, keeps the legacy name. The columns are unchanged.
The new AI_Chat_Bedrock_Insights::gap_window() accepts only an int, or a string of digits alone, equal to 7, 30 or 90. Anything else returns 30. The export handler reads the period only after the manage_options and nonce checks. The version is 1.48.0.
The controller ran the checks on commit f279e41. The feature test failed on the base commit, which lacks the feature, and passed on the candidate. On the candidate, bin/prerelease.sh passed: 40 suites, including admin-ux.php, insights.php and the earlier content-gap test test_feature_9ecd4de5ba50.php, which had failed in the prior attempt; phpcs was clean across 75 files. tests/tooling.php and bin/build-package.py also passed (89 files).

item.title: Decision coverage for recorded choices
item.description: How often does a recorded choice component answer when it abstains below a confidence threshold, and how often is it wrong? EvalArc 0.16.0 chooses the threshold on calibration decisions, then reports coverage and selective error on held-out decisions. Invalid responses stay visible instead of being counted as wrong answers.

item.title: Check a skill choice against the installed shortlist
item.description: Skills Anywhere 0.16.0 adds a two-step route command. Prepare builds a shortlist of installed skills that can actually be opened; apply checks a saved choice against that shortlist before it is used. The result says whether the pick is selected, absent, below the confidence threshold, stale or invalid. The command does not load or run the skill.

item.title: stall-threshold sensitivity for recorded step-limit failures
item.description: Adds --stall-sweep T1,T2,... to python -m robot_reel.stress. It re-labels verified recorded step-limit traces at up to eight stall thresholds in metres and reports per-threshold counts, changed and stable trials, and threshold-dependent boundaries against the unchanged 1 mm reference. No policy is re-run and no threshold is validated.

item.title: report consecutive-failure streak and failing_since date for struggling sources in pairadar.health
item.description: `python3 -m pairadar.health` now tells the maintainer and the nightly repair gate whether a struggling source has been continuously dark or is flapping. Each entry under `struggling` gains two fields next to the existing `source` and `failed_days`: `streak_days`, the number of consecutive runs (counted back from the latest run that recorded health inside the window) on which the source appears in `failed`, and `failing_since`, the `date` of the oldest run in that streak. A run on which the source answered, was served by its fallback endpoint, or was not attempted ends the streak. A new public helper `health.streak(runs, reference, window, source)` returns `(streak_days, failing_since)` and `(0, None)` when the source did not fail the latest run. All previously emitted keys (`reference`, `window_days`, `threshold_days`, `runs_with_health`, `failures`, `fallbacks`, and `source`/`failed_days` inside `struggling`), the worst-first ranking, the threshold and latest-run rules, and `--fail-on-struggling` exit codes are unchanged. The module docstring and docs/automation.md explain the two fields.
